_about: The 15 Field Notes and the one corrected note the owner approved on 15 November 2026 (wave 4, C4-05), copied character for character from the council file approved-local-facts.json. tools/build-facts.mjs adds the notes to its landmark list and writes each text over the bank explanation.

notes.text: The USGS says the park is best known for its 47 hot springs, which emerge from Hot Springs Mountain at an average temperature of 143 degrees Fahrenheit.
NPS calls the Hot Springs thermal springs the hottest east of the Rocky Mountains, and says they average 143 degrees Fahrenheit.
NPS says the Hot Springs thermal springs produce over 700,000 gallons of water a day.
Hot Springs has had three successive Arlington Hotel buildings, dating from 1875, 1892–93 and 1924.
The 1893 Arlington had 300 rooms, but only 50 had their own baths. It burned in 1923.
Radio station KTHS first broadcast from the Arlington Hotel.
Per Wikipedia, Hot Springs declared a city holiday for Oaklawn's first day of racing, and more than 3,000 people attended.
The first Arkansas Derby ran at Oaklawn Park in 1936 with a purse of $5,000.
Wikipedia says the Oaklawn meet, held December through May, is sometimes called the "Fifth Season".
Voters approved Amendment 100 in 2018, and Oaklawn became a full casino on April 1, 2019.
Arkansas Power & Light developed Lake Hamilton; Carpenter Dam, a concrete gravity dam, was completed in 1931 and the lake was created in 1932.
Wikipedia gives Lake Hamilton as about 7,200 acres; Lake Catherine, the smaller of the two lakes, is about 1,940 acres.
Lake Hamilton is named for Hamilton Moses, an Arkansas Power & Light executive; Carpenter Dam is named for Flavius Josephus Carpenter.
After Arkansas outlawed gambling in 1913, the Ohio Club on Central Avenue posed as the Ohio Cigar Store. A false wall hid the real club behind it.
According to Wikipedia, a Hot Springs casino revival during Gov. Orval Faubus's administration (1955-1967) was ended in 1967 by Republican Gov. Winthrop Rockefeller.
